title: On-Prem Usage Exporter & Delayed Sync for VPC Deployments
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Implement an on-prem usage collector and air-gapped export pipeline for Private/VPC deployments to ensure accurate billing, quota enforcement, and delayed sync to the central billing system when connectivity is restored. This ticket scopes the exporter format, integrity protections, reconciliation logic, and CLI/UX for manual export/import in regulated environments.

Why: Customers in VPC/on-prem and air-gapped environments cannot stream usage to the hosted billing pipeline. We need a robust, tamper-evident export and delayed-sync flow that preserves correctness (no double counting, idempotent imports), supports rate-limit reconciliation, and integrates with our billing pipeline with minimal operator work.

Goals:
- Define export data model and manifest format that supports delta exports and reconcilers.
- Build a lightweight on-prem collector daemon that aggregates token-level and event-level usage, produces signed gzipped exports, and exposes a local CLI for upload.
- Implement central import job that consumes exported bundles, validates signatures/manifests, reconciles against previously imported cursors, and emits billing events.
- Provide QA tests to validate clock skew, partial file transfers, repeated imports, and offline quota enforcement semantics.

Non-goals: Real-time streaming of usage from air-gapped clusters. Deep analytics for historical trends (handled after import).

Design notes:
- Export format: gzipped NDJSON with one usage event per line. Events are compacted by minute and include: local_sequence (monotonic per-instance), model_id, route, tokens_in, tokens_out, timestamp (UTC ISO8601), granule_id (UUID for grouping), and optional meta tags.
- Manifest: JSON metadata file with export_range (start/end timestamps), instance_id, export_id (UUID), expected_record_count, sha256 checksums for payload files, and a PKCS7 signature produced by the on-prem key pair.
- Signing: Support customer-provided key (recommended) or auto-generated key stored in local KMS. Signature prevents undetected tampering during offline transport.
- Transport: Two supported flows: 1) direct pull when connectivity available (collector pushes to central endpoint over mTLS); 2) air-gapped export file for manual transfer (S3-compatible bucket or operator USB).
- Idempotency: Central importer tracks import_cursor per instance_id + export_id combination. Duplicate uploads are ignored based on export_id. Partial uploads are rejected unless a complete manifest+payload checksums match.
- Reconciliation: Import job cross-checks incoming aggregates against expected billing windows to detect double-counting or missing deltas. Importer emits reconciliation report and marks records with reconciliation_status {ok, suspected_duplicate, gap_detected}.
- Offline quotas and rate limits: Local collector enforces soft limit using local counters and token buckets to provide the same developer experience. When offline, enforcement may be approximate; importer will surface overruns to billing but will not retroactively throttle.

Related artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PRIV/On-Prem+Usage+Exporter+Design
- Prototype repo: github.com/redwood-inference/onprem-usage-proto (branch: eng/collector)
acceptance_criteria: Collector daemon produces signed export bundles (manifest + payload) that validate via SHA256 and PKCS7 signature.
Central importer accepts export bundle and ingests events idempotently; import_cursor prevents duplicates.
Reconciliation report is generated after import showing total tokens, per-model breakdown, and any gaps or suspected duplicates.
Local collector enforces rate limits locally and exposes current counters/usage via /metrics and CLI.
End-to-end test covering manual file transfer (export -> import) with simulated clock skew and partial transfer recovery passes.
Documentation and operator CLI guide published in Private docs and linked in Console onboarding.
Security review completed and key management guidance added to the security playbook.

comments: 2026-02-11 Maya Chen: Kickoff meeting notes — agreed on gzipped NDJSON + manifest approach. Customer legal asked for tamper-evidence (PKCS7). See Confluence link.

2026-02-18 Liam O'Rourke: Prototype of collector created. CLI: redwood-usage export --since 2026-02-01 --until 2026-02-07 --out ./bundle.tar.gz. Proof-of-concept signature validated by central importer mock.
2026-02-24 Design review (PM + Security) feedback: require customer key option, must support HSM-backed keys in Private deployments. Updated design doc.
2026-03-03 Engineering sync: Decided to batch events by minute and include granule_id for easier shard-level reconcile. This reduces payload size ~6x in tests.
2026-03-08 QA: Created tests for repeated imports — importer idempotency logic passed on prototype for export_id dedup key.
2026-03-10 Security: Requested threat model review and rotation guidance for collector keys. Filed follow-up ENG-8745 for KMS integration work.
2026-03-12 Liam O'Rourke: Started central import implementation (PR opened) — https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4387
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal dogfood on staging private cluster; run 30-day retrospective and reconcile. Phase 2: opt-in beta with 3 customers; provide onboarding and manual import support. Phase 3: general availability with automation for direct pull when mTLS available. Monitor reconciliation reports and set SLA for import success rate.
test_plan: Unit tests for manifest validation and signature verification. Integration tests: simulate repeated upload, partial upload, and clock skew (+-5m and +-1h). End-to-end acceptance script that exports from collector, transfers bundle to a staging import endpoint, runs importer, and asserts billing events emitted match aggregated tokens.
notes: Edge cases: clock skew can cause overlapping export ranges — importer will dedupe by sequence numbers and export_id but will flag overlaps for manual review. If operator deletes manifests, import must fail fast and report missing files. Ensure export bundles are small enough for common USB transfers (<2GB) and support chunked exports for long windows. Consider future protobuf compact format for bandwidth-sensitive customers.
